qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Eastern US rail duopoly with Norfolk Southern provides core pricing power consistently 2-3% above rail cost inflation across ~20,000 route miles of physically unreplicable contiguous rights-of-way connecting major population centers and deep-water ports.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet). Irreplaceable eastern US rail duopoly (CAP = 15), but fails Gate 6 due to an overleveraged balance sheet (LT debt of $17.9B vs $3.47B Net Income = 5.15x, exceeding 4.0x ceiling), ongoing track maintenance capex ($2.5B) consistently exceeding depreciation ($1.65B) by 40-50%, past debt-funded buybacks, and macro-cyclical freight exposure with secular domestic coal runoff. [5-10Y g: volume 1.0% (net of coal decline) + price 2.5% + margin 0.5% + buybacks 2.5%]
qualitative.evidence: CSX operates ~20,000 route miles of irreplaceable rail infrastructure across 23 eastern US states and 2 Canadian provinces, forming an entrenched duopoly with Norfolk Southern. 2024 revenue of $14.0B spans Merchandise ($8.7B / 62%), Coal ($2.2B / 16%), Intermodal ($2.1B / 15%), and Trucking/Other ($1.0B / 7%). Operating margins averaged 37-41% over 2021-2024 (2024 Operating Income $5.25B, 37.5% margin; 2023 $5.50B, 37.5%; 2022 $5.95B, 40.1%). 5-year average GAAP ROIC has tracked 11.8-14.3% (2021: 15.1%, 2022: 15.3%, 2023: 14.3%, 2024: 13.5%), with persistent real core pricing power of 2-3% above rail cost inflation. FCF conversion is respectable (3-year average 82.6%; 2024 FCF $2.72B / NI $3.47B = 78.3%), but capital expenditures of $2.53B in 2024 and $2.26B in 2023 heavily exceed depreciation (~$1.65B), reflecting constant capital intensity to maintain right-of-way safety. Balance sheet leverage fails Gate 6: Long-term debt was $17.90B at year-end 2024 (total debt $18.50B) against $3.47B Net Income, resulting in LT Debt / Net Income of 5.15x (Net Debt / Net Income of 4.92x with $1.40B cash), far above the 4.0x ceiling, driven by past debt-funded share buybacks. Interest coverage remains solid at 6.3x (EBIT $5.25B / Interest $832M), but debt load, ongoing capex drain, and cyclical freight volumes fail the Munger peace-of-mind test.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
